findings.description: `_effort_on_wire` now unconditionally calls `cls.wire_effort(...)` for any adapter class returned by `adapter_class_for_type`. The prior implementation only handled CLI passthrough and Anthropic HTTP; other providers returned `None`. Unless every registered adapter class implements `wire_effort`, invoking a non-Anthropic provider with an effort value will raise `AttributeError` while emitting MODELINV completion telemetry.
findings.failure_mode: A request whose resolved hop has `effort` set but whose adapter class lacks `wire_effort` crashes during audit emission/result finalization instead of completing successfully.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the hook lookup, e.g. `wire_effort = getattr(cls, "wire_effort", None); return wire_effort(...) if callable(wire_effort) else None`, or add a default `wire_effort` classmethod to the adapter base class and ensure all registered adapters inherit it.

findings.description: In the `except ChevalError` branch, a hop whose error carries `failure_class: opt_in_required` is appended to `_models_not_planned`, but that hop is still present in `_modelinv_models_requested` (the agy-alone chain is deliberately left whole by `_plan_around_agy`) and it WAS dispatched (adapter.complete() ran and refused). The new `models_not_planned` parameter in `audit/modelinv.py:emit_model_invoke_complete` is documented as 'hops cheval did not plan (never dispatched)', and the test module docstring states a not-planned hop 'is not in models_requested'. The refusal path violates both: the same canonical appears in `models_requested` and `models_not_planned`, with `models_failed` empty.
findings.failure_mode: MODELINV records for an INVALID_CONFIG refusal show voices_planned=1, succeeded=0, failed=0, not_planned=[same hop]. Any verdict-quality or audit consumer that derives planned voices from `models_requested` and health from `models_failed` sees a planned voice that neither failed nor succeeded, and can label the record ok/APPROVED while the process exited INVALID_CONFIG. Double-membership also breaks any consumer that treats the two lists as disjoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the refused hop from `_modelinv_state['models_requested']` when recording it as not planned (so the two lists stay disjoint and the 'never dispatched' doc holds), or keep it in `models_failed` with `error_class: INVALID_CONFIG` and a distinct reason such as `refused_opt_in`, and update the modelinv.py docstring/schema enum accordingly.

findings.description: The reduced chain is rebuilt via `_RC(primary_alias=..., entries=kept, headless_mode=..., headless_mode_source=...)`, enumerating four fields by hand. Any other field on `ResolvedChain` (now or added later: capability/thinking class, ceiling policy, exhaustion reason, source metadata) is silently reset to its default on the re-planned chain only, with no test coverage because the test config exercises just these four.
findings.failure_mode: A future or existing optional field on ResolvedChain is dropped only when an agy hop was planned around, producing behaviour that differs between opt-in-on and opt-in-off runs of the same chain and is hard to trace.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `dataclasses.replace(chain, entries=kept)` (or an equivalent copy-with-entries helper on ResolvedChain) so every other field is carried over verbatim.

findings.description: The new loop validates `extra.reasoning_effort` against EFFORT_LEVELS (low|medium|high|xhigh|max) and emits a once-per-process WARN saying the value is 'ignored' when it does not match. `reasoning_effort` is the codex/grok adapters' own key and codex legitimately accepts `minimal`, which is not in EFFORT_LEVELS. For such an entry cheval now logs a misleading WARN, resolve_effort returns (None, 'none'), `_effort_on_wire` short-circuits on `effort is None`, so MODELINV records effort=None/effort_effective=None while the codex adapter still puts `minimal` on the wire from its own extra.
findings.failure_mode: Spurious config-smell WARN on a valid catalog entry, and MODELINV effort telemetry that contradicts what the adapter actually sent.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `reasoning_effort` against the owning adapter's accepted set (or only against the cheval set when the adapter is claude-headless), or extend the accepted values for that key; at minimum do not say 'ignored' for a key the adapter reads independently.

findings.description: `_plan_around_agy` is applied late, immediately before the MODELINV state is built, and the diff re-derives only `_auth_type_resolved` from the new primary. Under `prefer-cli` with the opt-in off, the original chain's primary is the agy hop; any other value derived from `_chain.entries[0]` before this point (effort resolution for the primary, dry-run output of the resolved model/chain, provider-config/adapter selection for the primary) was computed against a hop that will never be dispatched.
findings.failure_mode: `--dry-run` or pre-walk telemetry can report the agy hop as the resolved primary while the real walk dispatches the API hop, and primary-derived settings may reflect the wrong entry. Only the auth type is corrected.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the `_plan_around_agy` call to directly after chain resolution so every downstream consumer of `_chain` (dry-run, effort, auth type, adapter selection, MODELINV) sees the planned chain, and drop the special-case re-derivation of `_auth_type_resolved`.
